newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas rises across the curve, volumes greater.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas rises across the curve, volumes greater.

text.p: The natural gas futures market traded 155 lots on Wednesday morning, more than was traded in the whole of Monday and Tuesday combined.

Each of the five months from October to February saw a single trade, all of 25 lots. This led one futures broker to speculate that there may have been companies trading strips of more than one month, although given the confidential nature of the Energy Trading System, this could only be speculation.
"It's quite possible that it's strips," he said. "It's probably not five companies doing different things, more like one or two companies doing strips."

He added that this would be encouraging for the development of the contract, as it suggested players were not just looking at prices of single months but "ascertaining real value" by comparing prices of strips on the futures market with similar periods on the OTC market, where strip trading is common.

Prices were up where changed, with May, June, and November through to February all ticking up. January and February rose the most, up by 0.21 pence and 0.185 pence a therm respectively. February is now back over the psychologically important 17 pence a therm level, with the last deal done at 17.05 pence.
